references.text: The parallel text in [ref:Matt 19:16|Matthew 19:16] tells the same story where a man comes to Jesus and asks, "What good must I do to have eternal life?" Matthew identifies him as a young man, while Luke calls him a "ruler" (ἄρχων).

The parallel text in [ref:Mark 10:17|Mark 10:17] describes the same event where a man runs to Jesus, falls on his knees, and asks, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" Mark uses the same form of address "Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ" as Luke.

In [ref:Luk 10:25|Luke 10:25], a lawyer asks Jesus a similar question: "What must I do to inherit eternal life?" (τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω). The wording is almost identical to the ruler's question in 18:18.

In [ref:Joh 3:15-16|John 3:15-16], Jesus speaks of eternal life (ζωὴν αἰώνιον) as God's gift through faith in the Son. This expands on the theme of how one inherits eternal life, which the ruler asks about.

In [ref:Dan 12:2|Daniel 12:2], we find one of the clearest Old Testament references to eternal life, where it is said that many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, "some to eternal life." This forms the Old Testament background for the concept of "eternal life" that the ruler asks about.
In [ref:Apg 16:30|Acts 16:30], the jailer in Philippi asks a similar question: "What must I do to be saved?" This reflects the universal question of salvation that the ruler also asks in Luke 18:18.

In [ref:Luk 23:13|Luke 23:13], the word ἄρχων (ruler/leader) is used, the same word that describes the man who asked the question in 18:18. Luke uses this term to identify him as a person of high social status.

In [ref:5 Mos 6:24-25|Deuteronomy 6:24-25], obedience to the Lord's commands is linked with life and righteousness. This Old Testament idea that doing what is right leads to life underlies the ruler's question about what he must "do" to inherit eternal life.
